qns_content.text: A car moving at \( 54 \, \text{km/h} \) decelerates uniformly to rest. If it covers \( 37.5 \, \text{m} \) in the last \( 5 \, \text{s} \) before stopping, what is the deceleration?

text_solutions:
Convert speed: \( 54 \, \text{km/h} = 54 \cdot \frac{1000}{3600} = 15 \, \text{m/s} \).

Let deceleration = \( a \). Time to stop: \( t = \frac{v_0}{a} = \frac{15}{a} \).

Distance in last 5 s: \( x = v t + \frac{1}{2} a t^2 \), where \( v = a \cdot 5 \) (velocity 5 s before stopping).

Total distance: \( x_{\text{total}} = \frac{v_0^2}{2a} = \frac{15^2}{2a} = \frac{225}{2a} \).

Distance before last 5 s: \( x_{\text{total}} - 37.5 = v_0 (t - 5) + \frac{1}{2} a (t - 5)^2 \).

Simplify: \( 37.5 = 15 \cdot 5 - \frac{1}{2} a (5)^2 \Rightarrow 37.5 = 75 - 12.5 a \Rightarrow 12.5 a = 37.5 \Rightarrow a = 3 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

Deceleration = \( 3 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

Two balls are thrown upwards simultaneously from the ground with speeds \( 20 \, \text{m/s} \) and \( 30 \, \text{m/s} \). After how much time do they have the same velocity? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))

text_solutions:
Velocity: \( v_1 = 20 - 10 t \), \( v_2 = 30 - 10 t \).

Set \( v_1 = v_2 \): \( 20 - 10 t = 30 - 10 t \), not possible directly, so consider relative motion or when one overtakes.

Correction: They have same velocity magnitude when one is going up and other down. Time to max height: \( t_1 = 2 \, \text{s} \), \( t_2 = 3 \, \text{s} \).

After \( t_2 \), \( v_2 = 30 - 10 (t - 3) \) downward. At \( t = 5 \, \text{s} \): \( v_1 = 20 - 10 \cdot 5 = -30 \, \text{m/s} \), \( v_2 = 30 - 10 \cdot 2 = 10 \, \text{m/s} \) (no match).

Instead, equal velocity occurs at \( t = 1 \, \text{s} \) relative difference: \( v_1 = 10 \, \text{m/s} \), \( v_2 = 20 \, \text{m/s} \) (misstep). Correct: Equal magnitude opposite direction after \( t = 2 \, \text{s} \), \( v_2 = 10 \, \text{m/s} \) down at \( t = 4 \, \text{s} \), \( v_1 = -20 \, \text{m/s} \).

Time = \( 4 \, \text{s} \).

qns_content.text: Two masses \( 5 \, \text{kg} \) and \( 10 \, \text{kg} \) are \( 10 \, \text{m} \) apart. What is the gravitational potential at a point \( 4 \, \text{m} \) from the \( 5 \, \text{kg} \) mass? (\( G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \))

A \( 0.8 \, \text{kg} \) stone in a vertical circle of radius \( 2 \, \text{m} \) has a speed of \( 15 \, \text{m/s} \) at the bottom. What is the tension at the top if a \( 5 \, \text{N} \) tangential force acts? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))

text_solutions:
Bottom: \( T_b - mg = m v_b^2 / r \Rightarrow T_b - 0.8 \times 10 = 0.8 \times (15)^2 / 2 \).

\( T_b - 8 = 0.8 \times 112.5 \Rightarrow T_b - 8 = 90 \Rightarrow T_b = 98 \, \text{N} \) (tangential doesn’t affect radial).

Energy: \( \frac{1}{2} m v_b^2 - \frac{1}{2} m v_t^2 = 2mg \Rightarrow 0.4 \times 225 - 0.4 v_t^2 = 2 \times 0.8 \times 10 \).

\( 90 - 0.4 v_t^2 = 16 \Rightarrow 0.4 v_t^2 = 74 \Rightarrow v_t^2 = 185 \Rightarrow v_t \approx 13.6 \, \text{m/s} \).

Top: \( T_t + mg = m v_t^2 / r \Rightarrow T_t + 8 = 0.8 \times 185 / 2 \Rightarrow T_t + 8 = 74 \Rightarrow T_t = 66 \, \text{N} \).

qns_content.text: A \( 1200 \, \text{kg} \) car turns on a banked road (\( \theta = 25^\circ \), \( \mu_s = 0.25 \)) with radius \( 60 \, \text{m} \). What is the optimum speed to avoid friction? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( \tan 25^\circ \approx 0.466 \))

text_solutions:
Optimum speed occurs when banking alone provides centripetal force: \( v_0 = \sqrt{rg \tan\theta} \).

Substitute: \( r = 60 \, \text{m} \), \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( \tan 25^\circ = 0.466 \).

\( v_0^2 = 60 \times 10 \times 0.466 = 600 \times 0.466 = 279.6 \).

\( v_0 = \sqrt{279.6} \approx 16.72 \, \text{m/s} \).

qns_content.text: For the reaction \(\ce{H2(g) + Cl2(g) -> 2HCl(g)}\), if \(\Delta H = -184.6 kJ/mol\) at 298 K, what is \(\Delta U\) (R = 8.314 J/mol·K)?

text_solutions: \(\Delta n_g = 2 - (1 + 1) = 0\), so \(\Delta H = \Delta U + \Delta n_g RT = \Delta U\). \(\Delta U = -184.6 kJ/mol\).

text_solutions: Glucose (\( \ce{C6H12O6} \)) is the primary sugar in human blood, serving as a key energy source for cells.

qns_content.text: A gas has a solubility of 0.025 mol/L in water at a partial pressure of 5 bar at 298 K. What is the Henry's law constant (\( K_H \)) in bar?

text_solutions:
Henry's law: \( p = K_H \cdot \text{solubility (in molarity)} \).

\( K_H = \frac{p}{\text{solubility}} = \frac{5}{0.025} = 200 \, \text{bar} \).

qns_content.text: Which molecule has a bond order of 1.5 due to resonance?

text_solutions: In \( \ce{O3} \), resonance between two structures (one double, one single bond) averages the bond order to 1.5 per O-O bond.

qns_content.text: Which model of the atom resembles the solar system with electrons orbiting the nucleus?

text_solutions: Rutherford’s nuclear model likens the atom to a solar system, with electrons revolving around a central nucleus, unlike Thomson’s uniform sphere.

qns_content.text: How many grams of N₂ are required to produce 34 g of NH₃ in the reaction \( \ce{N2 + 3H2 -> 2NH3} \)? (Atomic masses: N = 14, H = 1)

text_solutions:
Molar mass of NH₃ = 17 g/mol.

Moles of NH₃ = 34 / 17 = 2 mol.

1 mol N₂ produces 2 mol NH₃. Moles of N₂ = 1 mol.

Mass = 1 × 28 = 28 g.

qns_content.text: Which molecule exhibits hydrogen bonding due to fluorine’s electronegativity?

text_solutions: \( \ce{HF} \) has hydrogen bonded to highly electronegative fluorine, enabling hydrogen bonding between molecules.

qns_content.text: Calculate the lattice enthalpy of NaCl if \(\Delta_f H^\circ(\text{NaCl}) = -411 kJ/mol\), \(\Delta_{sub} H^\circ(\text{Na}) = 108.4 kJ/mol\), \(\Delta_i H^\circ(\text{Na}) = 496 kJ/mol\), \(\frac{1}{2}\Delta_{bond} H^\circ(\text{Cl}_2) = 121 kJ/mol\), \(\Delta_{eg} H^\circ(\text{Cl}) = -348.6 kJ/mol\).

text_solutions: Using Born-Haber cycle: \(\Delta_f H^\circ = \Delta_{sub} H^\circ + \Delta_i H^\circ + \frac{1}{2}\Delta_{bond} H^\circ + \Delta_{eg} H^\circ - \Delta_{lattice} H^\circ\). \(-411 = 108.4 + 496 + 121 - 348.6 - \Delta_{lattice} H^\circ\). \(\Delta_{lattice} H^\circ = 788 kJ/mol\).

qns_content.text: Which of the following tests can distinguish between methanoic acid and ethanoic acid?

text_solutions: Methanoic acid gives a positive Tollens’ test due to the presence of an aldehyde-like hydrogen, while ethanoic acid does not.

qns_content.text: Which of the following has the shortest bond length?

text_solutions: Bond length decreases with increasing bond order. \( \ce{N2} \) (triple bond, 109 pm) is shorter than \( \ce{O2} \) (121 pm), \( \ce{F2} \) (144 pm), or \( \ce{Cl2} \) (199 pm).

qns_content.text: The element with atomic number 71 belongs to which series?

text_solutions: Lutetium (Lu, Z=71) has \([Xe] 4f^{14} 5d^1 6s^2\), marking the end of the lanthanoid series (4f filling).

qns_content.text: Which species can act as both a Bronsted acid and base?

text_solutions: \( \ce{HSO4-} \) can donate \( \ce{H+} \) (acid) or accept \( \ce{H+} \) (base).

qns_content.text: In the Carius method, which reagent is used to precipitate sulphur as \( \ce{BaSO4} \)?

text_solutions: Sulphur is oxidized to \( \ce{H2SO4} \), which reacts with \( \ce{BaCl2} \) to form a white precipitate of \( \ce{BaSO4} \) in the Carius method.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is the correct order of reactivity towards electrophilic addition reactions?

text_solutions: Due to the availability of pi electrons, alkenes are more reactive than alkynes in electrophilic addition reactions.

qns_content.text: Which type of isomerism is exhibited by \( \ce{CH3CH2OCH3} \) and \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2OH} \)?

text_solutions: Both have the formula \( \ce{C3H8O} \) but differ in functional groups (ether vs. alcohol), indicating functional isomerism.

text_solutions:
Empirical mass = 12 + 2 + 16 = 30 g/mol.

n = 60 / 30 = 2.

qns_content.text: What is the maximum number of emission lines when an electron drops from \(n = 5\) to the ground state in a hydrogen atom?

text_solutions: Number of emission lines = \(\frac{n(n-1)}{2}\), where \(n = 5\). So, \(\frac{5 \times 4}{2} = 10\).

qns_content.text: Which of the following is the most stable conformation of ethane?

text_solutions: The staggered conformation is more stable than the eclipsed conformation due to minimal torsional strain.

qns_content.text: Calculate the mole fraction of methanol (\( \ce{CH3OH} \)) in a solution containing 32 g of methanol and 144 g of water. (Molar mass: \( \ce{CH3OH} = 32 \, \text{g/mol}, \ce{H2O} = 18 \, \text{g/mol} \))

text_solutions:
Moles of methanol = \( \frac{32}{32} = 1 \, \text{mol} \).

Moles of water = \( \frac{144}{18} = 8 \, \text{mol} \).

Total moles = 1 + 8 = 9.

Mole fraction of methanol = \( \frac{1}{9} = 0.111 \).

qns_content.text: Which of the following ions is a strong oxidizing agent with a standard electrode potential of +1.74 V?

text_solutions: \( \ce{Ce^{4+}} \) has \( E^\circ = +1.74 \, \text{V} \) for \( \ce{Ce^{4+}/Ce^{3+}} \), making it a strong oxidant.

qns_content.text: Which of the following elements is classified as an inner-transition element?

text_solutions: Inner-transition elements (f-block) include lanthanoids and actinoids. Cerium (Ce, Z=58) has \(4f^1\), placing it in the f-block.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is the correct IUPAC name of chloroform?

text_solutions: Chloroform’s IUPAC name is trichloromethane, as it contains three chlorine atoms attached to a single carbon atom.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements is true about ethers?

options.text: Ethers have higher boiling points than alcohols
Ethers have lower boiling points than alcohols

text_solutions: Ethers do not exhibit hydrogen bonding among themselves, resulting in lower boiling points compared to alcohols of similar molecular weight.

qns_content.text: Which of the following compounds does not undergo the iodoform reaction?

text_solutions: The iodoform test is given by compounds containing the \(\ce{-COCH3}\) group. Benzaldehyde lacks this group and does not give the test.

qns_content.text: Which amine is formed when \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2CONH2} \) is treated with \( \ce{Br2} \) and \( \ce{NaOH} \)?

text_solutions: Hoffmann bromamide reaction of pentanamide (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2CONH2} \)) with \( \ce{Br2}/NaOH \) yields butan-1-amine (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2NH2} \)) by losing one carbon.

qns_content.text: Which of the following amines forms a salt soluble in excess \( \ce{NaOH} \) when treated with benzenesulphonyl chloride?

text_solutions: Primary amines like \( \ce{CH3NH2} \) form sulphonamides with benzenesulphonyl chloride that have an acidic hydrogen, making them soluble in excess \( \ce{NaOH} \) in the Hinsberg test.

qns_content.text: Which of the following compounds is isostructural with \( \ce{KClO4} \)?

text_solutions: \( \ce{KMnO4} \) forms crystals isostructural with \( \ce{KClO4} \), both having tetrahedral anions (\( \ce{MnO4^-} \) and \( \ce{ClO4^-} \)).

qns_content.text: What is the molality of a solution containing 5 g of urea (NH₂CONH₂) in 250 g of water? (Molar mass of urea = 60 g/mol)

text_solutions:
Moles = 5 / 60 = 0.0833 mol.

Mass of solvent = 0.25 kg.

Molality = 0.0833 / 0.25 ≈ 0.333 m.

qns_content.text: Which type of vascular bundle arrangement is present in roots?

text_solutions: In roots, vascular bundles are radial, where xylem and phloem are arranged on different radii.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is correct about the fluid mosaic model?

options.text: The plasma membrane is rigid and immovable.
Proteins are embedded in a phospholipid bilayer.
Only lipids are present in the membrane.

text_solutions: The fluid mosaic model describes the plasma membrane as a phospholipid bilayer with embedded proteins.

qns_content.text: Which plant growth regulator is commonly used to induce flowering in pineapple plants?

text_solutions: Ethylene is used to induce flowering and synchronize fruiting in pineapple plantations.

qns_content.text: During double fertilization, the sperm that fuses with the polar nuclei results in the formation of which structure?

text_solutions: The fusion of one sperm with the two polar nuclei forms the triploid endosperm, which provides nutrition to the embryo.

qns_content.text: Which process ensures that each gamete receives only one allele of a gene pair?

text_solutions: The principle of segregation ensures that alleles separate during gamete formation, allowing each gamete to receive only one allele of a gene pair.

qns_content.text: What is the primary difference between immigration and emigration?

options.text: Immigration decreases population size, emigration increases it
Immigration is movement into a population, emigration is movement out
Emigration refers to seasonal migration, immigration does not

text_solutions: Immigration is the movement of individuals into a population, while emigration is the movement of individuals out of it.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about keystone species is incorrect?

options.text: Keystone species have a significant impact on ecosystem structure.
Keystone species can be predators, herbivores, or mutualists.
Removing a keystone species has no effect on the ecosystem.

text_solutions: Keystone species play a crucial role in maintaining ecosystem balance, and their removal can lead to ecosystem collapse.

qns_content.text: Which checkpoint ensures that the DNA has been correctly replicated before mitosis begins?

text_solutions: The G2 checkpoint ensures that DNA replication is complete and accurate before the cell enters mitosis.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about phyllotaxy is incorrect?

text_solutions: Whorled phyllotaxy is not common in dicots; it is a special arrangement found in some plants like Alstonia.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is the primary criterion for classifying organisms into taxonomic categories?

text_solutions: Organisms are primarily classified based on morphological characteristics in taxonomy.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about the epidermal tissue system is correct?

options.text: The epidermis is usually single-layered and protects the plant.
Epidermal cells are dead at maturity and have thick walls.
Stomata are present in roots for gaseous exchange.
The cuticle is present in all plant organs, including roots.

text_solutions: The epidermis is a single-layered protective layer in plants. It is made up of living cells, and the cuticle is absent in roots.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is incorrect about lysosomes?

options.text: Lysosomes are called 'suicidal bags' of the cell.

text_solutions: Lysosomes do not synthesize lipids; they are involved in breaking down waste materials and cellular debris.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about meiosis I is correct?

text_solutions: In meiosis I, homologous chromosomes separate, reducing the chromosome number to haploid.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about the Z scheme of electron transport is correct?

options.text: Electrons move from PSII to PSI through an electron transport chain

text_solutions: In the Z scheme, electrons move from PSII to PSI via an electron transport chain, enabling ATP and NADPH production.

qns_content.text: Which chromosomal disorder results in an individual with a total of 47 chromosomes?

text_solutions: Klinefelter’s syndrome results from an extra X chromosome (47, XXY), leading to a total of 47 chromosomes.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about habitat destruction is correct?

options.text: Habitat destruction is a major cause of biodiversity loss.
Habitat destruction does not affect species survival.

text_solutions: Habitat destruction, including deforestation and urbanization, is a leading cause of species extinction and biodiversity loss.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a correct statement about the lac operon?

options.text: It codes for enzymes that digest lactose.
It is always active regardless of lactose presence.
It does not have a regulatory gene.

text_solutions: The lac operon codes for enzymes that help digest lactose and is regulated by a repressor.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about genetic mutations is incorrect?

options.text: Point mutations involve a change in a single nucleotide.
Missense mutations result in the formation of a stop codon.
Frameshift mutations occur due to insertions or deletions.
Nonsense mutations introduce a premature stop codon.

text_solutions: Missense mutations lead to a single amino acid change, while nonsense mutations create a stop codon.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about leaf modifications is correct?

options.text: Leaflets in neem are modified for climbing

text_solutions: Spines in xerophytic plants like cactus reduce the surface area, thereby minimizing transpiration.

qns_content.text: Which of the following groups contains members that lack chlorophyll and obtain nutrients through absorption?

text_solutions: Fungi lack chlorophyll and obtain nutrients through absorption, either as saprophytes or parasites.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about bulliform cells in monocot leaves is correct?

options.text: They help in leaf rolling under drought conditions.

text_solutions: Bulliform cells help in leaf rolling during water stress, reducing water loss in monocot leaves.

qns_content.text: Which part of the cell is responsible for controlling the entry and exit of substances?

text_solutions: The plasma membrane is selectively permeable and regulates the movement of substances in and out of the cell.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is true about interphase?

options.text: It is a resting phase with no metabolic activity
It includes G1, S, and G2 phases

text_solutions: Interphase consists of G1, S, and G2 phases, during which the cell grows, replicates DNA, and prepares for mitosis.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is INCORRECT about anaerobic respiration?

options.text: It produces ethanol or lactic acid as end products.
It generates more ATP than aerobic respiration.
It takes place in the absence of oxygen.

text_solutions: Anaerobic respiration generates much less ATP than aerobic respiration.

qns_content.text: Which of the following factors is essential for the seed germination process?

text_solutions: Oxygen is essential for releasing metabolic energy required for seed germination through respiration.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about the water cycle is incorrect?

options.text: Evaporation and transpiration contribute to atmospheric water vapor.
Groundwater movement is not part of the water cycle.

text_solutions: Groundwater movement is an important part of the water cycle, influencing water availability in ecosystems.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is an example of a grazing food chain?

text_solutions: A grazing food chain starts with living producers like grass or algae and is consumed by herbivores and carnivores.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about mutations is correct?

options.text: Silent mutations do not change the amino acid sequence.
Mutations always result in a change in protein function.

text_solutions: Silent mutations do not change the amino acid sequence due to the redundancy of the genetic code.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about stem modifications is correct?

text_solutions: Stolons are horizontal stems that grow along the soil surface, as seen in strawberry.

qns_content.text: Why do diatoms remain preserved in water bodies even after they die?

options.text: Their cell walls are made of silica

text_solutions: Diatoms have siliceous cell walls that do not decompose easily, leading to the formation of diatomaceous earth.

qns_content.text: Which organelle in prokaryotic cells is involved in DNA replication and distribution to daughter cells?

text_solutions: Mesosomes in prokaryotic cells are involved in cell wall formation, DNA replication, and distribution to daughter cells.

qns_content.text: Which enzyme is responsible for crossing over during meiosis?

text_solutions: Recombinase facilitates crossing over during the pachytene stage of prophase I in meiosis.

qns_content.text: What happens to excess light energy absorbed by chlorophyll?

options.text: It is dissipated as heat or fluorescence
It is used in the reduction of NADP⁺
It is used for photolysis of water

text_solutions: Excess light energy is dissipated as heat or fluorescence to prevent damage to the photosynthetic machinery.

qns_content.text: How many ATP molecules are produced through substrate-level phosphorylation during glycolysis?

text_solutions: In glycolysis, substrate-level phosphorylation directly generates 4 ATP molecules.

qns_content.text: Which of the following correctly describes codominance?

options.text: One allele is dominant over the other.
Both alleles contribute equally to the phenotype.
Only one allele is expressed at a time.

text_solutions: In codominance, both alleles are fully expressed, as seen in the AB blood group.

qns_content.text: Which enzyme is responsible for forming peptide bonds between amino acids during translation?

text_solutions: Peptidyl transferase is an enzyme that catalyzes the formation of peptide bonds between amino acids during translation.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is an incorrect statement about habitat fragmentation?

options.text: Habitat fragmentation can lead to population decline.
Habitat fragmentation is caused by deforestation and urbanization.

text_solutions: Habitat fragmentation typically reduces genetic diversity by isolating populations and limiting gene flow.

qns_content.text: Which law explains that alleles of a gene pair separate during gamete formation?

text_solutions: The Law of Segregation states that alleles separate during gamete formation and recombine in offspring.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about inflorescence is incorrect?

options.text: Racemose inflorescence has an acropetal flower arrangement
Cymose inflorescence has a continuously growing main axis
Umbel is a type of racemose inflorescence
Spadix is found in banana and maize

text_solutions: In cymose inflorescence, the main axis terminates in a flower and does not grow continuously.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about bryophytes is correct?

options.text: Bryophytes have true roots, stems, and leaves with vascular tissues.
Bryophytes are dependent on water for sexual reproduction.
The sporophyte in bryophytes is the dominant, free-living phase.
Bryophytes belong to the algae group Chlorophyceae.

text_solutions: Bryophytes require water for sexual reproduction, earning them the name 'amphibians of the plant kingdom'.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about fruits is incorrect?

options.text: Legumes do not split open at maturity
Aggregate fruits develop from multiple ovaries of a single flower

text_solutions: Legumes are dehiscent fruits that split open at maturity to release seeds.

qns_content.text: Where does non-cyclic photophosphorylation occur?

text_solutions: Non-cyclic photophosphorylation occurs in the thylakoid membrane, where both PSII and PSI are involved in electron transport.

qns_content.text: What is the function of the micropyle in an ovule?

options.text: To allow entry of the pollen tube

text_solutions: The micropyle is a small opening in the ovule that permits the entry of the pollen tube during fertilization.

qns_content.text: Which component of an operon serves as the binding site for a repressor protein?

text_solutions: The operator region of an operon serves as the binding site for a repressor protein, regulating gene expression.

qns_content.text: Which enzyme is responsible for the synthesis of ribosomal RNA (rRNA) in eukaryotes?

text_solutions: RNA polymerase I is responsible for synthesizing ribosomal RNA (rRNA) in eukaryotic cells.

qns_content.text: Which system in frogs consists of cranial, spinal, and autonomic nerves?

text_solutions: The nervous system in frogs consists of the central nervous system (brain and spinal cord), peripheral nervous system (cranial and spinal nerves), and autonomic nervous system.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about synovial joints is incorrect?

options.text: They allow a wide range of movement.

text_solutions: Synovial joints have cartilage on the articulating surfaces, which helps in smooth movement​.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about autoimmune diseases is incorrect?

options.text: Autoimmune diseases occur when the immune system attacks the body's own cells.
Autoimmune diseases are caused by viral infections.

text_solutions: Autoimmune diseases are not directly caused by viral infections; they result from immune system dysfunction.

qns_content.text: Which step in recombinant DNA technology ensures only transformed cells grow?

text_solutions: Selectable markers, such as antibiotic resistance genes, help distinguish transformed cells from non-transformed cells by allowing growth only in selective media.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is correct?

options.text: Mutation is the only source of genetic variation.
Genetic recombination increases genetic variability in populations.
Lamarck’s theory of evolution is based on natural selection.
Fossil records do not provide insights into evolutionary history.

text_solutions: Genetic recombination during sexual reproduction increases genetic variability in populations.

qns_content.text: Which of the following WBCs is the most abundant in human blood?

text_solutions: Neutrophils are the most abundant WBCs, constituting about 60-65% of total leukocytes.

qns_content.text: Which respiratory disorder is caused by chronic exposure to pollutants and results in inflammation of the bronchi?

text_solutions: Bronchitis is a respiratory disorder characterized by inflammation of the bronchi due to prolonged exposure to pollutants.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about ATP is incorrect?

options.text: ATP is the primary energy currency of cells.
ATP provides energy through the breakdown of peptide bonds.

text_solutions: ATP provides energy through the hydrolysis of phosphate bonds, not peptide bonds.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about nucleic acids is correct?

options.text: DNA and RNA are composed of amino acids.

text_solutions: RNA is usually single-stranded, while DNA is double-stranded and contains deoxyribose sugar.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is an example of a jawless fish?

text_solutions: Petromyzon (lamprey) is a jawless fish belonging to class Cyclostomata.

qns_content.text: Which statement about the composition of urine is incorrect?

options.text: Urine contains urea, creatinine, and uric acid.
Urine normally contains proteins and blood cells.
Urine composition varies depending on hydration and diet.

text_solutions: Normally, proteins and blood cells are not present in urine, as they are retained in the bloodstream.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about the Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act is correct?

options.text: MTP is allowed under specific medical conditions.
MTP is legally permitted for gender selection.
MTP can be performed without medical supervision.
MTP is a method of permanent contraception.

text_solutions: The MTP Act allows termination of pregnancy under specific medical conditions to protect the health of the mother or in cases of fetal abnormalities.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is correct about restriction enzymes?

options.text: Restriction enzymes are used to join DNA fragments.
Restriction enzymes cut DNA at specific recognition sites.

text_solutions: Restriction enzymes act as molecular scissors that cut DNA at specific recognition sequences, essential in genetic engineering.

qns_content.text: Which hormone is primarily responsible for stimulating the growth and development of ovarian follicles in the early menstrual cycle?

text_solutions: FSH stimulates the growth and maturation of ovarian follicles during the follicular phase of the menstrual cycle.

qns_content.text: Which hormone is responsible for stimulating the adrenal cortex to produce cortisol?

text_solutions: ACTH, secreted by the anterior pituitary, stimulates the adrenal cortex to produce cortisol.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about the autonomic nervous system is correct?

options.text: It controls involuntary functions such as digestion and heart rate.
It consists of only the parasympathetic division.
It has no effect on blood pressure regulation.

text_solutions: The autonomic nervous system regulates involuntary functions such as digestion, respiration, and heart rate.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about the human respiratory system is correct?

options.text: The right lung has three lobes, while the left lung has two lobes.

text_solutions: The right lung consists of three lobes, whereas the left lung has two lobes to accommodate the heart.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about ATP is correct?

options.text: ATP is an energy carrier in cells.

text_solutions: ATP is the main energy carrier in cells. It is not an enzyme, does not contain peptide bonds, and can be regenerated.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about frog metamorphosis is correct?

options.text: Frog metamorphosis is controlled by the thyroid hormone.
Frogs do not have a larval stage.
Frog eggs hatch directly into small frogs.
Metamorphosis in frogs occurs inside the mother’s body.

text_solutions: Thyroid hormones play a crucial role in the metamorphosis of tadpoles into adult frogs.

qns_content.text: Why are hemichordates considered an intermediate group between non-chordates and chordates?

options.text: They have a stomochord, functionally similar to a notochord
They show a complete digestive system like arthropods

text_solutions: Hemichordates possess a stomochord in the collar region, which is similar in function to the notochord but structurally different. This places them between non-chordates and chordates.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about DNA polymerase is incorrect?

options.text: DNA polymerase adds nucleotides in a 3' to 5' direction.
DNA polymerase is used in DNA replication.
Taq polymerase is a thermostable DNA polymerase.

text_solutions: DNA polymerase synthesizes new DNA in the 5' to 3' direction, not 3' to 5'.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is correct regarding ELISA?

options.text: ELISA is used to detect proteins and antigens in samples.
ELISA is a method of gene cloning.
ELISA is used to amplify RNA sequences.

text_solutions: ELISA (Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay) is used to detect the presence of proteins, antigens, and antibodies in biological samples.

qns_content.text: Which of the following substances is commonly abused by athletes to enhance muscle strength?

text_solutions: Anabolic steroids are commonly abused by athletes to enhance muscle strength and performance.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: Analogous organs have a common evolutionary origin.
Adaptive radiation leads to species diversity from a common ancestor.
Paleontology is the study of DNA sequences.

text_solutions: Adaptive radiation results in species diversity as organisms adapt to different ecological niches from a common ancestor.

qns_content.text: What is capacitation in sperm?

options.text: The process by which sperm gain the ability to fertilize the oocyte
The initial formation of sperm in the testes
The maturation of sperm in the epididymis

text_solutions: Capacitation is the physiological process that sperm undergo in the female reproductive tract, which enables them to penetrate and fertilize the oocyte.

qns_content.text: Which type of movement occurs when the foot is pointed downward?

text_solutions: Plantar flexion is the movement that points the foot downward, such as when standing on tiptoes.

qns_content.text: Which of the following structures is responsible for the removal of nitrogenous waste in insects?

text_solutions: Malpighian tubules are the excretory structures in insects, helping in nitrogenous waste removal and osmoregulation.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about phospholipids is incorrect?

options.text: Phospholipids are major components of cell membranes.
Phospholipids have hydrophobic tails and hydrophilic heads.
Phospholipids are involved in the genetic coding process.

text_solutions: Phospholipids are structural components of membranes but are not directly involved in genetic coding.

qns_content.text: Which chamber of the frog’s heart pumps oxygenated blood?

text_solutions: The single ventricle of the frog’s heart pumps a mix of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood to the body.

qns_content.text: Which characteristic of amphibians limits their distribution to moist environments?

text_solutions: Amphibians require moist environments because they undergo external fertilization and have aquatic larval stages.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about hypertension is incorrect?

options.text: It is a condition of persistently high blood pressure.
It can lead to stroke, heart disease, and kidney failure.
It is commonly measured using a sphygmomanometer.

text_solutions: Hypertension is influenced by diet, physical activity, and lifestyle factors. Healthy habits can help prevent it.

qns_content.text: Which of the following muscles is responsible for the movement of the eyeball?

text_solutions: The rectus muscles control the movement of the eyeball in different directions.

qns_content.text: Which human ancestor had a brain capacity of around 900 cc and used fire?

text_solutions: Homo erectus had a brain capacity of around 900 cc and was the first to use fire.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about lymph nodes is correct?

options.text: Lymph nodes filter lymph to remove pathogens.
Lymph nodes store oxygen for body tissues.

text_solutions: Lymph nodes filter lymph and help trap pathogens, playing a key role in immune defense.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about gel electrophoresis is incorrect?

options.text: Gel electrophoresis separates DNA fragments based on size.
DNA fragments move toward the negative electrode.
Smaller DNA fragments migrate faster than larger ones.
Agarose gel electrophoresis is commonly used for DNA separation.

text_solutions: DNA is negatively charged and moves toward the positive electrode (anode) in gel electrophoresis.

qns_content.text: Which component is essential for initiating the Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR)?

text_solutions: Primers are short sequences of nucleotides essential for initiating DNA synthesis in PCR.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a role of human placental lactogen (hPL) during pregnancy?

options.text: Alters maternal metabolism to favor fetal nutrition

text_solutions: hPL modifies maternal metabolism to increase nutrient availability for the developing fetus.

qns_content.text: Which condition is caused by the hyposecretion of thyroid hormones in adults?

text_solutions: Myxedema is caused by hypothyroidism in adults, leading to lethargy, weight gain, and slow metabolism.

qns_content.text: Which type of nerve fiber transmits impulses from tissues and organs to the central nervous system?

text_solutions: Afferent fibers transmit sensory impulses from tissues and organs to the CNS.

qns_content.text: Which phylum includes animals with an open circulatory system and hemocoel?

text_solutions: Arthropods have an open circulatory system where blood flows into a hemocoel instead of being confined to vessels.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a major symptom of rabies?

text_solutions: Rabies causes hydrophobia (fear of water), muscle spasms, and neurological complications.

qns_content.text: Which enzyme helps in linking insulin polypeptide chains during recombinant insulin production?

text_solutions: Disulfide isomerase helps form disulfide bonds between the A and B chains of insulin during recombinant insulin production.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about genetically modified organisms (GMOs) is correct?

options.text: GMOs are developed using recombinant DNA technology.
GMOs are always harmful to the environment.

text_solutions: GMOs are developed using recombinant DNA technology and have applications in agriculture, medicine, and biotechnology.

qns_content.text: What is the term for the process by which new species evolve from existing species through accumulated changes?

text_solutions: Speciation refers to the formation of new species through evolutionary changes in populations over time.

qns_content.text: Which of the following contraceptive methods involves the use of chemicals to kill sperms?

text_solutions: Spermicidal creams contain chemicals that kill sperms, thereby preventing fertilization.
